# sources


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module finds text, files it in the vault, and checks it. It imports
from `abhyasa.learner` and `abhyasa.models`. It has four parts:

- **Grounding**: the passages from your vault that a question or a
  lesson stands on, and the words that name an idea.
- **Sources**: read a paper, a page, a folder or a repo, and file it in
  your vault.
- **Read what you typed**: what the Start box finds in your words: a
  link, a paper, a folder, a repo or a goal.
- **Check a web source**: which search results research may read, the
  real search and fetch, and the check that a quote is word for word and
  about the idea.

Import the modules that this module uses. The heavy ones load inside the
functions that need them, so the import stays light.

## Grounding

Your sources for grounding, and the links from each concept to your own
work.

The tutor writes better questions when it can see what you read and what
you did. This module gives it that view.

- A *source* finds short passages for a query. It reads only.
- [`ground`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#ground)
  asks every source and merges the passages.
- [`Learning.connect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#learning.connect)
  keeps the best passages for a concept as its links: where the concept
  shows up in your work.
- [`index_notebooks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#index_notebooks)
  puts the notebooks of a folder that you attach to a walk on a vault
  shelf, so every tool can search them.

These are the imports of the module.

### Passages

A passage is one short piece of text and where it came from. `src` names
the source, `ref` points into it, and `url` opens it when there is a
page for it.

### passage

``` python
def passage(
    src, ref, title, text, url:str='', **kw
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*One passage from a source.*

A cut text ends with `…`, so you can see that it is cut. A link keeps
where a passage is, with no text. The label of a passage adds the kind
of text and the place, when the passage has them.

``` python
test_eq((clip('abc def', 5), clip('abc', 5), clip(None, 5)), ('abc d…', 'abc', ''))
p0 = passage('notes', 'n1', 'DDPM notes', 'Noise.', section='2 Training', what='Summary', n=1)
test_eq(cite(p0), '[notes › DDPM notes · Summary · 2 Training]')
test_eq(link_of(p0), dict(src='notes', ref='n1', title='DDPM notes', url='', section='2 Training', what='Summary'))
test_eq(cite(passage('vault:notes', 'n1', 'My notes', 'x')), '[vault:notes › My notes]')
```

### Ground a query

[`ground`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#ground)
asks each source for passages and takes them in turn, so one source
cannot fill the list.

[`main_words`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#main_words)
gives the words of a query that carry its sense: three letters or more,
and not a small word such as *the* or *with*.
[`named_count`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#named_count)
counts how many of them a text names as whole words. A source with
`subjects` is for those subjects. For another subject,
[`ground`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#ground)
keeps only its passages whose text names every main word of the query,
so a verse never grounds an idea on U-nets.

### ground

``` python
def ground(
    q:str, sources, k:int=3, must:tuple=(), subject:str | None=None, floor:float=0.0, about:str | None=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Up to `k` passages for `q`, taken from the sources in turn. With
`must`, a passage must name one of those terms.* With `subject`, a
source with `subjects` that do not hold it gives only the passages that
name every main word of `q`. With `floor`, a passage must have a
[`relevance`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#relevance)
to `about` (default `q`) of `floor` or more, and keeps it as `score`.
When no passage passes, there is none: a weak match is no source.

### names

``` python
def names(
    p, terms
)->bool:
```

*Whether passage `p` names one of `terms` as a whole word, in its title
or its text.*

Two stand-in sources give numbered passages.
[`ground`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#ground)
takes them in turn.

``` python
class Src:
    def __init__(self, name, n): self.name, self.n = name, n
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L(passage(self.name, str(i), f'{self.name}{i}', q) for i in range(self.n))[:k]
test_eq(ground('x', [Src('a', 3), Src('b', 1)], k=3).attrgot('title'), ['a0', 'b0', 'a1'])
```

A link must name the concept.
[`names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#names)
compares whole words without marks, so a passage on *anumāna* links to
`Anumana`, and a passage on *rank fusion* does not link to `rank`.

``` python
test_eq(fold('Anumāna'), 'anumana')
assert names(passage('s', '1', 'Nyāya notes', 'On anumāna and vyāpti.'), ['Anumana'])
assert not names(passage('s', '1', 'Notes', 'ranked lists'), ['rank'])
test_eq(ground('x', [Src('alpha', 3)], k=3, must=['alpha1']).attrgot('title'), ['alpha1'])
```

A concept with a Devanagari name links to a passage that names it. Each
Devanagari word folds to its ASCII key, so the whole-word match works.
Another word does not match.

``` python
test_eq((fold('संधि'), fold('Vowel संधि: a + a → ā')), ('samdhi', 'vowel samdhi: a + a → a'))
assert names(passage('s', '1', 'संधि नियम', 'स्वर संधि में दो स्वर मिलते हैं।'), ['संधि'])
assert names_idea('संधि', [], 'स्वर संधि में दो स्वर मिलते हैं।')
assert not names(passage('s', '1', 'Notes', 'धर्म और अर्थ'), ['संधि'])
```

A Latin text with marks folds as before. A letter with no ASCII form,
such as `ß`, and the punctuation now stay, on both sides of a match, so
a whole word still matches.

``` python
import unicodedata
```

``` python
old = lambda s: unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', s or '').encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode().lower()
for t in ('Anumāna', 'Vyāpti and pramāṇa', 'naïve', 'LoRA, VAE', '', None): test_eq(fold(t), old(t))
test_eq(fold('Straße — naïve “quotes”'), 'straße — naive “quotes”')
assert names(passage('s', '1', 'Notes', 'Die Straße ist lang.'), ['Straße']) and not names(passage('s', '1', 'Notes', 'Die Strae ist lang.'), ['Straße'])
```

The main words of a name leave out the small words.
[`named_count`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#named_count)
counts whole words only, so *noisy* is not *noise*. A plural with `s` or
`es` counts.

``` python
test_eq(main_words('Fine-tune with LoRA on the Mac'), ['fine', 'tune', 'lora', 'mac'])
test_eq(named_count('We add noise with a noise schedule.', ['noise', 'schedule', 'unet']), 2)
test_eq(named_count('A noisy picture.', ['noise']), 0)
test_eq(named_count('The latents of the VAE.', ['latent', 'vae']), 2)   # a plural counts
```

A step name can be a sentence. Then
[`names_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#names_idea)
asks for a key term of the idea word for word, such as `LoRA`, and at
least half of the other main words of the name. A light plural stem lets
*updates* match *update*. A text with only one word of the name is a
weak match. A name with no key term other than itself still needs each
of its main words.

``` python
test_eq([stem(w) for w in ('updates', 'matches', 'class', 'weights', 'focus')], ['update', 'match', 'class', 'weight', 'focus'])
test_eq(key_terms('LoRA trains small low-rank updates'), ['LoRA trains small low-rank updates', 'LoRA'])
hf = 'Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models (LoRA) It adds pairs of rank-decomposition weight matrices (called update matrices) to existing weights, and only trains those newly added weights.'
assert names_idea('LoRA trains small low-rank updates', [], hf)   # LoRA, and 4 of the 5 other words
assert not names_idea('LoRA trains small low-rank updates', [], 'LoRA makes comic pictures in one style.')   # LoRA alone is weak
assert names_idea('Noise at step t', [], 'We add noise at each step.')   # no key term: each main word, as before
assert names_idea('Softmax', [], 'The softmax function.') and not names_idea('Make the Ramayana comic', [], 'A comic skit.')
```

A source with `subjects` is asked for its own subjects. For an ML idea,
it keeps only a passage that names every main word.

``` python
class Verses:
    name, subjects = 'verses', ('sanskrit',)
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('verses', 'a1', 'Ashtadhyayi 3.3.124', 'A rule on the net of words.'), passage('verses', 'a2', 'Notes', 'The U-net architecture.')])
test_eq(ground('U-net architecture', [Verses()], 2, subject='ml').attrgot('ref'), ['a2'])
test_eq(ground('U-net architecture', [Verses()], 2, subject='sanskrit').attrgot('ref'), ['a1', 'a2'])
test_eq(len(ground('U-net architecture', [Verses()], 2)), 2)   # with no subject, there is no gate
test_eq(ground('Ashtadhyayi rule', [Verses()], 2, subject='ml'), [])   # the title of a verse does not count
```

With `floor`, a passage that names too few main words of the question
goes. An unrelated verse that a full-text search found for one common
word is no source:

``` python
class Mixed:
    name = 'vedicreader'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('vedicreader', 'r1', 'Rigveda 05 061 070', 'The Maruts get the gifts of the bar of gold.'),
                                       passage('vedicreader', 'r2', 'Notes', 'Alpha bar t is the share of the signal that is left.')])
test_eq(relevance(Mixed().search('')[0], 'alpha bar diffusion'), 1/3)
ps = ground('alpha bar diffusion', [Mixed()], 3, floor=.5)
test_eq((ps.attrgot('ref'), ps[0].score), (['r2'], .667))
test_eq(ground('alpha bar', [Mixed()], 3, floor=.5, about='Kamba Ramayanam'), [])   # none passes: no passage
```

### Passages as data in a prompt

[`concept_grounds`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#concept_grounds)
gives up to `k` passages that name a concept, as a lesson uses them, and
never raises.
[`fence`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#fence) puts
one passage between `<source>` markers, so the model reads it as data.
Marker text in the passage is cut, so a false closing marker cannot end
the data early.
[`fenced`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#fenced)
does this for each passage.

``` python
test_eq(concept_grounds(dict(name='Anumana'), None), [])
```

### Links from a concept to your work

`connect` searches the sources for one concept and keeps the best five
passages in the `seen_in` meta of the concept. It does not keep the
text, only the place of the text, so the links stay small.

### find_notebooks

``` python
def find_notebooks(
    roots
):
```

*Every `.ipynb` under
[`roots`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#roots).*

Two notebooks in a temporary folder: one in a `notes` folder and one
beside it. A third notebook in `.venv` is skipped. The first run indexes
both.

``` python
from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb
```

``` python
lr, root = temp_learning(), Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(root/'proj/notes').mkdir(parents=True); (root/'proj/.venv').mkdir()
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# RRF notes', 'markdown'), mk_cell('1 + 1')]), root/'proj/notes/a.ipynb')
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('x = 1')]), root/'proj/b.ipynb')
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('y = 2')]), root/'proj/.venv/c.ipynb')
test_eq(sorted(p.name for p in find_notebooks([root])), ['a.ipynb', 'b.ipynb'])
test_eq(index_notebooks(lr.vault, [root]), dict(notebooks=2, changed=2, failed=0, same=0))
t = ' '.join(c['content'] for c in lr.vault.shelf('notebooks').store())
assert '# RRF notes' in t and '```python\n1 + 1\n```' in t   # the markdown, and the code in a fence
```

A second run reads no notebook again. A notebook that changes is read
again.

``` python
test_eq(index_notebooks(lr.vault, [root]), dict(notebooks=2, changed=0, failed=0, same=2))
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('x = 2')]), root/'proj/b.ipynb'); os.utime(root/'proj/b.ipynb', (1e9, 1e9))
test_eq(index_notebooks(lr.vault, [root]), dict(notebooks=2, changed=1, failed=0, same=1))
```

`files` gives the notebooks to file, in place of a search under
[`roots`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#roots). A
folder source uses it, so it decides which files are safe to read.

``` python
test_eq(index_notebooks(lr.vault, (), files=[root/'proj/b.ipynb']), dict(notebooks=1, changed=0, failed=0, same=1))
```

### The sources together

With the notebooks shelf in the vault,
[`VaultSource`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#vaultsource)
finds notebooks too. `connect` then links a concept to them.

``` python
lr.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Merge ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank).', 'ml', aliases=['RRF'])
links = lr.connect('reciprocal-rank-fusion', [VaultSource(lr)])
assert any(l['src'] == 'vault:notebooks' for l in links), links
assert not lr.stale_links(lr.concept('reciprocal-rank-fusion'))
```

The hits of all the shelves are sorted by score before the cut. Before
this, a shelf with one web page gave its page first for each query. Here
a web page on pet training and three course notebooks are in the vault.
The notebook on DDPM training comes first.

``` python
vl = temp_learning()
vl.vault.add('Dogs need daily training and walks. A web page about pets and their training at home.', 'Pet training tips', source='https://example.com/pets', kind='web')
for t, x in [('nbs/15_DDPM', 'DDPM training: we add noise with a noise schedule and train a model to predict the noise.'),
             ('nbs/17_DDPM_v2', 'A second version of the DDPM notebook with a cleaner noise schedule.'),
             ('nbs/26_diffusion_unet', 'A U-net predicts the noise in diffusion models.')]:
    vl.vault.shelf('notebooks').add(x, title=t, source=f'/tmp/course22p2/{t}.ipynb', kind='notebook', meta=dict(root='course22p2'))
test_eq(VaultSource(vl).search('DDPM training')[0].title, 'nbs/15_DDPM')
```

The search reads only the shelves of documents. A store of names, such
as `entities`, has no `docs` table. The search does not count its
documents, so SQLite logs no error, and the notebook still comes first.

``` python
import logging
```

``` python
class _Seen(logging.Handler):
    def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.got = []
    def emit(self, r): self.got.append(r.getMessage())
vl.vault.db.get_graph('store', ann=False)   # the store of names, as vishalakshi makes it
seen, root = _Seen(), logging.getLogger()
root.addHandler(seen)
try: test_eq(VaultSource(vl).search('DDPM training')[0].title, 'nbs/15_DDPM')
finally: root.removeHandler(seen)
test_eq([m for m in seen.got if 'no such table' in m], [])
```

## Sources

Add concepts to the concept graph from any text and from a vault
document.

This module adds concepts to the `learning` shelf. A model finds the
core ideas in a text, and code merges them with the concepts on the
shelf. The tutor then asks about the concepts that this module adds.

These are the imports of the module.

### Extraction from text

The model lists the core ideas of a text. Each idea has a true,
self-contained statement and its prereqs. Code does the merge. When a
slug or an alias matches a concept on the shelf, it is the same concept.
The lists of that concept get the new items, and its learner state does
not change.

`EXTRACT_SP` and
[`extract_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract_prompt)
ask the model for the concepts. The model also gives the section, one
quote, the figure, the ways that suit the idea, and the people and
dates. The model also gives a group path. The prompt lists the groups of
the subject, so the tree does not split into many groups with almost the
same name.
[`add_group`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#add_group)
adds the new groups of a reply for the next window.
[`quoted`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#quoted) puts
each name on one line in JSON quotes, so a name cannot add a line to the
prompt. The prompt says when an idea gets `order`, `demo` or `code`,
because a walk gives an idea with one of these ways a check of that
kind. `EXTRACT_SP` is a registered prompt, so you can change it on the
Settings page.

The prompt asks for the ideas that a learner must understand, not for
facts to test. Each idea gets `core`, the understanding in 1 or 2
sentences (what it does and why), and `wrong`, 1 to 3 common wrong
ideas. A number, a year, a score, an ablation, a remark of the author or
a history line is a *detail*: it comes with `detail: true`, so a walk
can show it as reading and not check it.

[`_index`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_index)

page, because the vault counts pages from 0 and a reader counts from 1.

[`doc_pages`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#doc_pages)
returns the chunks of a document. When the main shelf has no such
document, it looks on the other shelves, but not on the `learning` shelf
of your concepts.

[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
adds the concepts of a text. When it gets pages, it also keeps where
each idea is in the text: the order, the section, the page and the
passage.
[`_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#_read) asks
the model for each window.
[`_places`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_places)
puts the ideas in the order of the text.
[`from_vault`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#from_vault)
does the same for one document of the vault.

[`math_cut`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#math_cut)
cuts a text to a length, but never inside a formula. A cut inside `$…$`
or `$$…$$` moves back to before the formula, so a cut passage or a cut
page never shows half a formula. An escaped `\$` is not a formula mark.
A web page can have a `$` that is a price: a cut never moves back more
than `MATH_MOST` characters, so a page does not lose its text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L352"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### math_cut

``` python
def math_cut(
    s:str, n:int
)->str:
```

*`s` cut to at most `n` characters, never inside a `$…$` or `$$…$$`
formula: a cut in a formula moves back to before it. A `$` more than
`MATH_MOST` characters back is not a formula.*

A cut in an inline or a block formula moves back to before it. A cut
after a whole formula, or in text with an escaped `\$`, stays where it
is.

``` python
f = r'We scale by $\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$ here.'
test_eq(math_cut(f, 20), 'We scale by '); test_eq(math_cut(f, len(f) - 1), r'We scale by $\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$ here')
test_eq(math_cut('A $$x=1$$ and $$y=2$$.', 18), 'A $$x=1$$ and ')
test_eq(math_cut(r'Pay \$5 and \$6 now.', 12), r'Pay \$5 and ')
test_eq(math_cut('$a$$b$ c', 5), '$a$'); test_eq(math_cut('short', 10), 'short')
test_eq(len(math_cut('It costs $5. ' + 'x' * 5000, 3000)), 3000)   # a price far back: the cut stays
```

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### extract

``` python
def extract(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, text:str='', subject:str='', source:dict=None, pages:list=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Add the core ideas of `text` (or of `pages`, a list of `(page, text)`)
to the shelf as concepts, merged with the concepts there. Return the
slugs that it changed.*

A fake model returns three concepts. One matches `Ranking` on the shelf
by its alias `rank`.

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
lr.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml', aliases=['rank'])
fake = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[
    dict(name='Reciprocal rank fusion', statement='Sum 1/(k + rank) over lists.', aliases=['RRF'], prereqs=['rank', 'Ranked list'],
         core='It merges ranked lists so that an item high in any list scores well, because 1/(k + rank) falls fast with rank.',
         wrong=[dict(think='it averages the raw scores', fact='it uses only the ranks')]),
    dict(name='Ranked list', statement='Items in score order.', aliases=[], prereqs=[], detail=True),
    dict(name='Ranking', statement='Ordering by score.', aliases=['ordering'], prereqs=[])])})
```

[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
returns the changed slugs. The prereqs become slugs, and the old concept
gets the new alias and statement.

``` python
test_eq(sorted(extract(lr, fake, 'some text', 'ml', dict(src='test'))), ['ranked-list', 'ranking', 'reciprocal-rank-fusion'])
test_eq(lr.concept('reciprocal-rank-fusion').prereqs, ['ranking', 'ranked-list'])
test_eq(lr.concept('ranking').aliases, ['rank', 'ordering'])
test_eq(lr.concept('ranking').statement, 'Ordering by score.')
```

Each idea keeps its `core` and its wrong ideas. A detail has `detail`
set, so a walk shows it as reading.

``` python
rrf = lr.concept('reciprocal-rank-fusion')
assert rrf.core.startswith('It merges ranked lists') and not rrf.detail
test_eq(rrf.wrong, [dict(think='it averages the raw scores', fact='it uses only the ranks')])
assert lr.concept('ranked-list').detail
```

### The core of an old idea

A concept from an older version, or from a plan, can have no `core`.
[`understand`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#understand)
writes its `core` and its wrong ideas from its statement and its
passage, with one model call, and saves them. A concept that has a
`core` makes no call. When the model fails, the concept stays as it is.
The prompt `core` is a registered prompt.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L457"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### understand

``` python
def understand(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, c
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Concept `c` (a slug or a dict) with its `core` and `wrong`: as it is
when it has a `core`, else written by the model and saved. A failure
keeps it as it is.*

An idea with no `core` gets one from the model, with its wrong ideas. A
second call finds the `core` and asks nothing.

``` python
ul = temp_learning(); ul.put('Softmax', 'Softmax maps scores to weights that sum to 1.', 'ml')
fk = Fake({'Return JSON: {"core"': dict(core='Softmax turns any scores into weights that add up to 1, so they can act as shares.', wrong=['the biggest score gets all the weight'])})
u = understand(ul, fk, 'softmax')
assert u.core.startswith('Softmax turns') and u.wrong[0]['think'].startswith('the biggest')
n = len(fk.calls); understand(ul, fk, 'softmax'); test_eq(len(fk.calls), n)
```

A reply with no `core` changes nothing.

``` python
ul.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit')
assert not understand(ul, Fake(), 'sandhi').get('core')
```

[`_windows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_windows)
cuts at paragraph breaks.

``` python
test_eq(len(_windows('a\n\n' * 10, size=5)), 5)
```

#### A group for each new concept

The model also gives each new concept a group path under the subject.
The prompt lists the groups that the subject has now, so a new concept
goes into one of them when it fits. Here the subject has a group from
the tutor and a group that the learner made by hand.

``` python
gl = temp_learning()
gl.put('Ashvini', 'The first nakshatra.', 'jyotisha', group=['nakshatras'], group_by='model')
gl.put('Magha', 'The tenth nakshatra.', 'jyotisha', group=['Nakshatras', 'Gana'], group_by='hand')
gfake = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[
    dict(name='Bharani', statement='The second nakshatra.', group=['jyotisha', 'nakshatras']),
    dict(name='Magha', statement='The tenth nakshatra, ruled by Ketu.', group=['rasis']),
    dict(name='Ashvini', statement='The first nakshatra.', group=['stars']),
    dict(name='Lagna', statement='The rising sign.', group=['Signs', 'Rising', 'More'])])})
test_eq(sorted(extract(gl, gfake, 'some text', 'jyotisha')), ['ashvini', 'bharani', 'lagna', 'magha'])
```

The prompt asks for the group and lists the groups of the subject, with
their parents.

``` python
p = gfake.calls[0][0]
assert '"group": [str]' in p and 'Groups of this subject now: nakshatras; Nakshatras › Gana' in p, p
```

A new concept gets its group, cleaned: the subject drops. When the
subject has groups, the group must be one of them, spelled the same way;
else the concept has no group. A concept that has a group keeps it. A
concept that you moved by hand stays.

``` python
test_eq((gl.concept('bharani').group, gl.concept('bharani').group_by), (['nakshatras'], 'placed'))   # the subject has groups: placed by the tutor
test_is(gl.concept('lagna').get('group'), None)   # `Signs` is a new group: the tutor does not make it by itself
test_eq(gl.concept('ashvini').group, ['nakshatras'])
test_eq((gl.concept('magha').group, gl.concept('magha').group_by), (['Nakshatras', 'Gana'], 'hand'))
```

#### A subject and a readable name for each new concept

When the learner gives no subject, the finder gives one for each idea: a
subject that exists, or a short new one. All ideas of one text get one
subject, unless an idea clearly belongs to another subject that exists.
A concept that has a subject keeps it. A name that is empty, or is a
slug, becomes words.

``` python
sx = temp_learning(); sx.put('Rope', 'A position code.', 'physics')
srep = dict(concepts=[dict(name='Softmax', statement='Scores to weights.', subject='Transformers'),
    dict(name='attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution', statement='Heads.', subject='transformers'),
    dict(name='', statement='A rank is a position in a list.'), dict(name='Rope', statement='Again.', subject='ml')])
sxf = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': srep})
test_eq(sorted(extract(sx, sxf, 'text')), ['a-rank-is-a-position-in', 'attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution', 'rope', 'softmax'])
test_eq([sx.concept(s).subject for s in ('softmax', 'attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution', 'a-rank-is-a-position-in', 'rope')], ['transformers', 'transformers', 'transformers', 'physics'])
test_eq(sx.concept('attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution').name, 'Attention heads and anaphora resolution')
test_eq(sx.concept('a-rank-is-a-position-in').name, 'A rank is a position in')
assert 'Subjects the learner has: "physics"' in sxf.calls[0][0] and '"subject": str' in sxf.calls[0][0]
```

With a subject from the learner, the finder is not asked for one, and
each new concept gets the subject of the learner.

``` python
sy = temp_learning(); syf = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': srep})
extract(sy, syf, 'text', 'ml')
test_eq({c.subject for c in sy.concepts()}, {'ml'})
assert '"subject": str' not in syf.calls[0][0] and 'Subjects the learner has' not in syf.calls[0][0]
```

A subject from the learner is cleaned (short, plain, lower case) before
it goes in the prompt, in quotes, and on the concepts.

``` python
sz = temp_learning(); szf = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': srep})
extract(sz, szf, 'text', ' ML  Stuff!\n- evil: x ')
test_eq({c.subject for c in sz.concepts()}, {'ml stuff - evil x'})
assert 'Subject: "ml stuff - evil x"\n' in szf.calls[0][0] and not any(l.startswith('- evil') for l in szf.calls[0][0].splitlines())
```

### Reading order and where each idea stands

When the text comes as pages,
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
also keeps the order, the section, the page and the passage of each
idea. These tests use a small paper in a temporary vault. The paper data
is in `tests/walk_data.py`.

A fake model names three ideas of the paper.
[`from_vault`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#from_vault)
returns them in the order of the text.

``` python
lr = temp_learning(); did = add_paper(lr)
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': EXTRACT_REPLY})
slugs = from_vault(lr, ask, did)
test_eq(list(slugs), ['sequential-computation', 'softmax', 'scaling-by-the-root-of-dk'])
```

The placement of an idea is in its provenance. The page is the page a
reader sees: the vault counts pages from 0, so the stored page 3 is page
4.

``` python
p = placement(lr.concept('softmax'), did)
test_eq((p.order, p.section, p.page), (1, '3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention', 4))
assert p.passage.startswith('apply a softmax function')
test_eq(p.figure, 'attention/images/fig2.png')
```

The way fields, the picture and the people go on the concept.

``` python
test_eq(lr.concept('softmax').ways, ['code', 'maths'])
test_eq(lr.concept('softmax').visual, True)
test_eq(lr.concept('softmax').image, 'attention/images/fig2.png')
test_eq(lr.concept('scaling-by-the-root-of-dk').who, ['Vaswani'])
```

A second document that names Softmax keeps its own placement. The ways
of the two documents merge.

``` python
d2 = lr.vault.add([(0, 'Softmax gives weights.')], 'Notes', source='/tmp/notes.md', kind='file')['doc_id']
from_vault(lr, Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[dict(name='Softmax', statement='', quote='Softmax gives weights.', section='', ways=['words'])])}), d2)
test_eq(placement(lr.concept('softmax'), did).page, 4)
test_eq(placement(lr.concept('softmax'), d2).page, 1)
test_eq(lr.concept('softmax').ways, ['code', 'maths', 'words'])
```

A quote that is not in the text gives no passage. A figure file that is
not there gives no figure.

``` python
bad = dict(concepts=[dict(name='Masking', statement='The decoder hides later positions.', quote='we mask out all values', figure='images/nope.png', section='3.2.3')])
lr2 = temp_learning(); d3 = add_paper(lr2); from_vault(lr2, Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': bad}), d3)
m = placement(lr2.concept('masking'), d3)
test_eq((m.passage, m.span, m.figure), ('', None, None))
```

A long paper has 15 pages. The model sees the paper in windows, and the
last idea still gets its page.

``` python
long = [(i, f'{i + 1} Section {i + 1}\n\n' + f'Idea {i + 1} is stated here. ' * 140) for i in range(15)]
lr3 = temp_learning(); d4 = lr3.vault.add(long, 'Long paper', source='/tmp/long.pdf', kind='pdf')['doc_id']
def per_window(p, sp):
    ns = sorted({int(n) for n in re.findall(r'Idea (\d+) is stated', p)})
    return json.dumps(dict(concepts=[dict(name=f'Idea {n}', statement=f'Idea {n}.', quote=f'Idea {n} is stated here.', section=f'{n} Section {n}') for n in ns]))
from_vault(lr3, per_window, d4)
test_eq(placement(lr3.concept('idea-15'), d4).page, 15)
```

[`locate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#locate)
folds white space and case. It refuses a quote that is too short.

``` python
pg = [(1, 'One two.\n\nThree   FOUR five six.'), (2, 'Seven eight nine ten.')]
test_eq(locate(pg, 'three four FIVE six'), (1, 10, 31))
test_eq(locate(pg, 'seven eight nine'), (2, 0, 16))
test_is(locate(pg, 'three'), None)
test_is(locate(pg, 'nothing of this is there'), None)
```

[`figure_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#figure_path)
keeps a figure only when the file is there, stays in the assets folder
of that one document and has an image suffix. The folder of a PDF link
is named by the last part of the link, such as `1706.03762`, which
`Path.stem` would cut to `1706`.

``` python
test_eq(figure_path(lr, '/tmp/attention.pdf', 'images/fig2.png'), 'attention/images/fig2.png')
test_is(figure_path(lr, '/tmp/attention.pdf', '../../../etc/hosts'), None)
test_is(figure_path(lr, '/tmp/attention.pdf', '/etc/hosts'), None)
(lr.vault.assets('attention')/'images'/'x.txt').write_text('x')
test_is(figure_path(lr, '/tmp/attention.pdf', 'images/x.txt'), None)
(lr.vault.assets('1706.03762')/'images'/'page3_1.png').parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (lr.vault.assets('1706.03762')/'images'/'page3_1.png').write_bytes(b'x')
test_eq(figure_path(lr, 'https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762', 'images/page3_1.png'), '1706.03762/images/page3_1.png')   # a link, not a file
(lr.vault.assets('other')/'images').mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (lr.vault.assets('other')/'images'/'o.png').write_bytes(b'x')
test_is(figure_path(lr, '/tmp/attention.pdf', '../other/images/o.png'), None)   # the image of another document
test_is(figure_path(lr, '/tmp/..', 'assets/other/images/o.png'), None)          # a source with no name of its own
test_is(figure_path(lr, '/', 'other/images/o.png'), None)
```

### Sort your concepts into groups

An old vault has no groups. The Concepts page has the action “Sort my
concepts”. It asks the model to place the concepts of each subject in a
tree of at most two levels. The model reads about `lists.sort_batch`
concepts in each request. Each request lists the groups so far, so the
batches use the same groups.
[`propose_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#propose_groups)
saves nothing: the page shows the tree, and
[`apply_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#apply_groups)
saves it when the learner accepts it. Neither one changes a concept that
the learner moved by hand.

`SORT_SP` and
[`sort_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#sort_prompt)
ask for the place of each concept in one batch.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L481"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### sort_prompt

``` python
def sort_prompt(
    subject:str, cs, groups:tuple=(), subjects:tuple=(), again:bool=False, closed:bool=False, every:bool=False
)->str:
```

*The request for one batch: the subject (or the subjects that exist, for
concepts with no subject), the groups so far, and one line for each
concept. `again` asks for the concepts that got no place. `closed`
allows only a group from the list: any other answer is \[\]. `every`
says that the sort starts again, and that the groups in the list are the
groups that the learner made.*

[`propose_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#propose_groups)
asks for each subject in batches and returns `{slug: path}`.
[`apply_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#apply_groups)
saves the paths that change. The sort uses the model of the concept
finder.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L545"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### place_new

``` python
def place_new(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, batch:int=None
)->list:
```

*Place the new concepts of each subject that has groups: one request for
each batch, and no second request. A concept that fits no group of the
list, that has no subject, or that you undid stays. Return the slugs
placed.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L523"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### apply_groups

``` python
def apply_groups(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, places:dict, every:bool=False, free:tuple=(), unmark:tuple=()
)->list:
```

*Save the paths of `places` as a saved sort, and keep the group list of
each subject. A concept with no subject gets its proposed subject first.
Return the slugs that moved. A concept that has a group, that you moved
by hand, or that is gone, stays. With `every`, a concept with a group
moves too, and so does a concept that you moved by hand when it is in
`free`; the group list of each subject becomes the new groups and the
hand groups. `unmark` (`(subject, path)`) takes the hand mark off those
groups first. It is one step: when a write fails, it writes all back and
raises.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L497"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### propose_groups

``` python
def propose_groups(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, subject:str=None, batch:int=None, only:NoneType=None, closed:bool=False,
    every:bool=False, free:tuple=()
)->__main__.Places:
```

*Ask the model for the group of each concept that has no group (and that
you did not keep out of the groups by hand), `batch` concepts at a time
for each subject; ask again once for the concepts that got no place.
Concepts with no subject also get one. A concept with a group never
moves. `only` limits it to these slugs. With `closed`, a group must be
in the list of the subject, spelled the same way, and it asks one time
for each batch; any other answer leaves the concept out. With `every`,
it sorts every concept again, except a concept that you moved by hand
and that is not in `free`, and the list of groups is only the hand
groups. Save nothing.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L493"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Places

``` python
def Places(
    *a, subjects:NoneType=None, left:NoneType=None
):
```

*The result of a sort: `{slug: group}`, with `.subjects`
(`{slug: subject}` for concepts that had none) and `.left` (the slugs
that got no place).*

These tests use five nakshatras, one concept that the learner moved by
hand, and one concept in another subject. The fake model puts each
concept that it sees in a group, and it also names a concept that it did
not get and a concept that is not there.

``` python
sl = temp_learning()
for k in range(5): sl.put(f'Nakshatra {k}', f'Star {k}.', 'jyotisha')
sl.put('Magha', 'The tenth nakshatra.', 'jyotisha'); sl.set_group('magha', 'mine')
sl.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit')
def sorter(p, sp):
    slugs = re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M)
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=['Nakshatras', f'Part {s[-1]}'] if s.startswith('nakshatra') else ['sound']) for s in slugs]
                + [dict(slug='magha', group=['taken']), dict(slug='nope', group=['x'])])
sfake = Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': sorter})
places = propose_groups(sl, sfake, batch=2)
```

Five free nakshatras in batches of 2 give three requests, and Sanskrit
gives one. The concept moved by hand is not in a request and not in the
result. A slug that the model makes up does not count.

``` python
test_eq(len(sfake.calls), 4)
test_eq(sorted(places), ['nakshatra-0', 'nakshatra-1', 'nakshatra-2', 'nakshatra-3', 'nakshatra-4', 'sandhi'])
test_eq((places['nakshatra-3'], places['sandhi']), (['Nakshatras', 'Part 3'], ['sound']))
assert not any('- magha:' in p for p, _ in sfake.calls)
test_eq(sfake.calls[0][1], prompt('concepts.sort'))
```

The first request lists the group that the learner made. A later request
also lists the groups of the batches before it.

``` python
assert 'Groups of this subject now: mine' in sfake.calls[0][0]
assert 'Nakshatras › Part 0' in sfake.calls[1][0]
```

Nothing is saved before the accept.
[`apply_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#apply_groups)
saves the tree and returns the slugs that it moved. It does not move the
concept that you moved by hand.

``` python
test_is(sl.concept('nakshatra-0').get('group'), None)
test_eq(sorted(apply_groups(sl, {**places, 'magha': ['taken'], 'nope': ['x']})), sorted(places))
test_eq((sl.concept('nakshatra-0').group, sl.concept('nakshatra-0').group_by), (['Nakshatras', 'Part 0'], 'sort'))
test_eq(sl.concept('magha').group, ['mine'])
test_eq(apply_groups(sl, places), [])
```

With a `subject`, the sort reads only that subject. A reply that is not
a list of places gives nothing.

``` python
f2 = Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': sorter})
sl.put('Visarga', 'A breath sound.', 'sanskrit')                  # `sandhi` is sorted now: only the new concept is asked
test_eq(list(propose_groups(sl, f2, 'sanskrit')), ['visarga'])
test_eq(propose_groups(sl, Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': '[1, 2]'}), 'sanskrit'), {})
```

A name or a statement with a line break and a leading `-` stays on its
own line, in quotes. So it cannot add a concept to the list. The known
names of the concept finder are quoted in the same way.

``` python
ql = temp_learning()
ql.put('Evil\n- injected: Fake', 'One.\n- other: Two', 'x', slug='evil')
p = sort_prompt('x', ql.concepts())
test_eq([l for l in p.splitlines() if l.startswith('- ')], ['- evil: "Evil - injected: Fake". "One. - other: Two"'])
p = extract_prompt('text', 'x', ['a\n- b'])
assert 'Concepts the learner already has: "a - b"' in p and not any(l.startswith('- b') for l in p.splitlines())
```

#### Every concept gets a place

The model can leave a concept out of its reply, or give it an empty
group. After each batch,
[`propose_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#propose_groups)
asks one more time, with only those concepts. A concept that still has
no place stays out of the result, and its slug is in `.left`.

First, a reply that leaves out one slug. The second request has only
that slug.

``` python
mk = temp_learning()
for k in range(3): mk.put(f'Star {k}', f'Star {k}.', 'jyotisha')
seen = []
def leaves_out(p, sp):
    slugs = re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M); seen.append(slugs)
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=['Stars']) for s in slugs if not (s == 'star-1' and len(seen) == 1)])
out = propose_groups(mk, Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': leaves_out}))
test_eq(seen, [['star-0', 'star-1', 'star-2'], ['star-1']])
test_eq((sorted(out), out.left), (['star-0', 'star-1', 'star-2'], []))
```

An empty group, or a group that is only the subject, also starts the
second request. When the second reply is still empty, the concept is
left out, and the model is not asked a third time.

``` python
seen.clear()
def empty(p, sp):
    slugs = re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M); seen.append(slugs)
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=[] if s == 'star-1' else ['Stars']) for s in slugs])
out = propose_groups(mk, Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': empty}))
test_eq(seen, [['star-0', 'star-1', 'star-2'], ['star-1']])
test_eq((sorted(out), out.left), (['star-0', 'star-2'], ['star-1']))
seen.clear()
def same(p, sp):
    slugs = re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M); seen.append(slugs)
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=['Jyotisha'] if s == 'star-1' and len(seen) == 1 else ['Stars']) for s in slugs])
out = propose_groups(mk, Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': same}))
test_eq((len(seen), out.left, out['star-1']), (2, [], ['Stars']))
```

The prompt asks for a group for every concept, with a short `Other`
group as the last resort.

``` python
sp = prompt('concepts.sort')
assert 'Other' in sp and 'Use [] for a concept' not in sp
```

#### A subject for a concept that has none

For concepts with no subject, the model also gives a subject: one that
exists, in its own spelling, or a new short one. The sort asks about
them as one batch. A concept that you moved by hand is not in it.

``` python
ns = temp_learning()
ns.put('Rasi', 'A sign.', 'jyotisha'); ns.put('Attention', 'Weights.'); ns.put('Softmax', 'Scores to weights.'); ns.put('Pinned', 'Mine.'); ns.set_group('pinned', 'mine')
who = dict(attention='Jyotisha', softmax='  Transformers!')
def subj(p, sp):
    slugs = re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M)
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=['Stars'], **({'subject': who[s]} if s in who else {})) for s in slugs])
sfk = Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': subj})
out = propose_groups(ns, sfk)
test_eq((out['attention'], out.subjects), (['Stars'], dict(attention='jyotisha', softmax='transformers')))
assert 'Subjects now: "jyotisha"' in sfk.calls[0][0] or 'Subjects now: "jyotisha"' in sfk.calls[1][0]
assert not any('- pinned:' in p for p, _ in sfk.calls) and 'pinned' not in out
```

The accept sets the subject first, as a move by the model, and then the
group. A concept that you moved by hand keeps both, also when a result
names it.

``` python
test_eq(sorted(apply_groups(ns, out)), ['attention', 'rasi', 'softmax'])
test_eq((ns.concept('attention').subject, ns.concept('attention').group), ('jyotisha', ['Stars']))
test_eq((ns.concept('softmax').subject, ns.concept('softmax').subject_by), ('transformers', 'model'))
forced = Places({'pinned': ['q']}, subjects=dict(pinned='x'))
test_eq(apply_groups(ns, forced), [])
test_eq((ns.concept('pinned').subject, ns.concept('pinned').group), ('', ['mine']))
```

#### Saved groups are locked

A sort only works on the concepts that have no group. A concept with a
group stays where it is, and the groups that a sort saved stay in the
list. The request has the group names of the subject, and the prompt
tells the model to use one of them first.

``` python
lk = temp_learning()
for k in range(3): lk.put(f'Star {k}', f'Star {k}.', 'jyotisha')
lk.put('Rasi', 'A sign.', 'jyotisha')
lk.set_group('star-0', ['Stars'], by='sort'); lk.set_group('rasi', ['Signs'], by='model'); lk.save_groups('jyotisha')
lseen = []
def lsorter(p, sp):
    sl_ = re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M); lseen.append((sl_, p))
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=['Stars']) for s in sl_])
lf = Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': lsorter})
out = propose_groups(lk, lf)
test_eq([s for s, _ in lseen], [['star-1', 'star-2']])                 # only the two with no group
assert 'Groups of this subject now: Signs; Stars' in lseen[0][1]
assert 'Use a group from the list' in prompt('concepts.sort') and 'first' in prompt('concepts.sort')
```

The accept marks each concept as set by a saved sort and keeps the group
list. A concept that got a group in the meantime does not move.

``` python
lk.set_group('star-2', ['Mine too'], by='placed')
test_eq(sorted(apply_groups(lk, out)), ['star-1'])
test_eq((lk.concept('star-1').group, lk.concept('star-1').group_by, lk.concept('star-2').group), (['Stars'], 'sort', ['Mine too']))
test_eq(lk.saved_groups('jyotisha'), [['Mine too'], ['Signs'], ['Stars']])      # the saved list has the groups in use
```

#### New concepts get a place by themselves

[`place_new`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#place_new)
places the new concepts of a subject that has groups. It makes one
request for each batch, not one for each concept, and it asks no second
time. It uses only a group that is in the list of the subject, spelled
the same way. Any other answer, `Other` too, leaves the concept in
`Not sorted yet`. A concept that you undid stays too.

``` python
for k in range(3): lk.put(f'New {k}', f'New {k}.', 'jyotisha')
lk.put('Lone', 'No subject.'); lk.put('Gone', 'Undone.', 'jyotisha'); lk.set_group('gone', ['Stars'], by='placed'); lk.unplace('gone')
lseen.clear()
def lfit(p, sp):
    sl_ = re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M); lseen.append((sl_, p))
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group={'new-2': ['Other'], 'new-1': ['stars']}.get(s, [' Stars '])) for s in sl_])
lf2 = Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': lfit})
test_eq(place_new(lk, lf2), ['new-0'])                                   # `Other` is not in the list, and `stars` is not `Stars`
test_eq([s for s, _ in lseen], [['new-0', 'new-1', 'new-2']])                # one batch, and no second ask
test_eq((lk.concept('new-0').group, lk.concept('new-0').group_by), (['Stars'], 'placed'))
test_eq([lk.concept(s).get('group') for s in ('new-1', 'new-2', 'lone')], [None, None, None])
test_eq(lk.concept('gone').group, [])
assert 'Other' not in lk.groups('jyotisha') and ['Stars'] in lk.groups('jyotisha') and len(lk.groups('jyotisha')) == 3
```

A concept that
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
adds to a subject with groups gets its group from the finder, marked as
placed by the tutor, only when the group is in the list of the subject,
spelled the same way. In a subject with no groups, the mark is `model`.
A name such as `x` is not made.

``` python
ex = temp_learning(); ex.put('Ashvini', 'The first.', 'jyotisha', group=['stars'], group_by='sort')
exf = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[dict(name='Bharani', statement='The second.', group=['stars']), dict(name='x', statement='A letter.'),
                                                       dict(name='Krittika', statement='The third.', group=['Stars']), dict(name='Rohini', statement='The fourth.', group=['Other'])])})
test_eq(sorted(extract(ex, exf, 'text', 'jyotisha')), ['bharani', 'krittika', 'rohini'])
test_eq([ex.concept(s).get('group') for s in ('krittika', 'rohini')], [None, None])   # `Stars` is not `stars`, and `Other` is not in the list
test_eq((ex.concept('bharani').group, ex.concept('bharani').group_by), (['stars'], 'placed'))
assert ex.concept('x') is None
extract(ex, Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[dict(name='Atom', statement='Small.', group=['bits'])])}), 'text', 'physics')
test_eq(ex.concept('atom').group_by, 'model')
```

#### Races

A placement is one step under a lock, and it looks at the concept again
just before the write. If you undo, or sort the concept yourself, while
the model works, the placement changes nothing. An undone concept is not
placed again, also by a later
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract).
A re-import or a later `put` does not change a group that a saved sort,
a placement or you set.

``` python
rc = temp_learning()
for k in range(3): rc.put(f'Card {k}', f'Card {k}.', 'deck')
rc.set_group('card-0', ['Aces'], by='sort'); rc.save_groups('deck')
def meddle(p, sp):
    rc.update('card-1', group=[], group_by='undone')                                                       # you undo during the call
    rc.set_group('card-2', ['Aces'], by='sort')                                                              # you sort it during the call
    return dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=['Aces']) for s in re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M)])
test_eq(place_new(rc, Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': meddle})), [])
test_eq([(rc.concept(s).get('group'), rc.concept(s).get('group_by')) for s in ('card-1', 'card-2')], [([], 'undone'), (['Aces'], 'sort')])
test_eq(place_new(rc, Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': meddle})), [])                         # `undone`: not placed again
test_eq(extract(rc, Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[dict(name='Card 1', statement='Again.', group=['Aces'])])}), 'text', 'deck'), ['card-1'])
test_eq((rc.concept('card-1').get('group'), rc.concept('card-1').group_by), ([], 'undone'))
```

``` python
for by, g in (('sort', ['Aces']), ('placed', ['Aces']), ('hand', ['Mine'])):
    rc.set_group('card-1', g, by=by)
    rc.put('Card 1', 'Again.', 'deck', slug='card-1', group=['Elsewhere'], group_by='model')      # a re-import, as from vedicreader
    test_eq((rc.concept('card-1').group, rc.concept('card-1').group_by), (g, by))
```

#### Sort everything again

`propose_groups(every=True)` sorts every concept of a subject again. A
concept that you moved by hand stays, except when its slug is in `free`:
you let the tutor sort it too. The request lists only the groups that
you made. `apply_groups(every=True)` saves the new tree and makes the
group list again. The hand groups stay in the list.

``` python
se = temp_learning()
for n in ('H1', 'H2'): se.put(n, f'{n}.', 'ml')
for n in ('S1', 'S2', 'S3'): se.put(n, f'{n}.', 'ml', group=['Old'], group_by='sort')
se.save_groups('ml'); se.new_group('ml', 'H')
for s in ('h1', 'h2'): se.set_group(s, ['H'])
sef = Fake({'Return JSON: {"places"': lambda p, sp: dict(places=[dict(slug=s, group=['New']) for s in re.findall(r'^- ([a-z0-9-]+):', p, re.M)])})
p = propose_groups(se, sef, 'ml', every=True)
test_eq(sorted(p), ['s1', 's2', 's3'])
assert 'Groups of this subject now: H\n' in sef.calls[-1][0] and 'Sort all these concepts again' in sef.calls[-1][0]
```

The accept moves the sorted concepts. The hand concepts stay, and the
old group goes from the list.

``` python
test_eq(sorted(apply_groups(se, p, every=True)), ['s1', 's2', 's3'])
test_eq((se.concept('h1').group, se.concept('s1').group, se.concept('s1').group_by), (['H'], ['New'], 'sort'))
test_eq(se.groups('ml'), [['H'], ['New']])
```

When you untick a group, its concepts are in `free`, and the tutor sorts
them too.

``` python
p = propose_groups(se, sef, 'ml', every=True, free=['h1', 'h2'])
test_eq(sorted(apply_groups(se, p, every=True, free=['h1', 'h2'])), ['h1', 'h2'])
test_eq((se.concept('h1').group, se.concept('h1').group_by), (['New'], 'sort'))
```

The accept is one step. When a write fails in the middle, the concepts,
the group list and the hand marks are as they were before.

``` python
at = temp_learning()
for n in ('A1', 'A2'): at.put(n, f'{n}.', 'ml', group=['Old'], group_by='sort')
at.save_groups('ml'); at.new_group('ml', 'Mine'); at.set_group('a2', ['Mine'])
calls = []
def breaks(slug, path, by='hand'):
    calls.append(slug)
    if len(calls) > 1: raise RuntimeError('the disk is full')
    return Learning.set_group(at, slug, path, by)
at.set_group = breaks
test_fail(lambda: apply_groups(at, {'a1': ['New'], 'a2': ['New']}, every=True, free=['a2'], unmark=[('ml', ['Mine'])]), contains='disk is full')
del at.set_group
test_eq([(at.concept(s).group, at.concept(s).group_by) for s in ('a1', 'a2')], [(['Old'], 'sort'), (['Mine'], 'hand')])
test_eq((at.hand_groups('ml'), at.saved_groups('ml')), ([['Mine']], [['Mine'], ['Old']]))
```

### From a link

You can give a link: an arXiv id or a PDF link, a docs page, or a GitHub
repo or file.
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link)
files its pages in the vault, and the walk reads them in order. abhyasa
fetches a link only when you send the form, and only the link that you
give. A crawl stays in the folder of the link and stops at the page cap.

The Links group of the settings sets the limits of a link: `links.cap`
is the most pages that one link can give, `links.kept` is the most
characters of one page that the vault keeps, and `links.read` is the
most that the tutor reads.
[`fetch_opts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#fetch_opts)
gives the limits of each fetch from the settings: a time limit and a
speed limit, so one page cannot be larger than 30 MB with the defaults.
It also gives `allow_private=False`, so that fossick refuses a private
address on each fetch, also when `FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE` is set for
Leela or for a test. vishalakshi’s `url_folder` (here `link_folder`)
gives the folder of a link, and `in_scope` tells if a link is in it.
`Vault.crawl(scope=)` follows only the links in that folder.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L559"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### fetch_opts

``` python
def fetch_opts()->dict:
```

*The limits of one fetch, from the settings: the time limit, the speed
cap in bytes a second and one retry. `allow_private=False` refuses a
private address also when `$FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE` is set.*

[`link_kind`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#link_kind)
names the reader for a link, as `fossick.what_is` does. It takes only an
arXiv id, or an http or https link to a host on the internet. The app
must not fetch its own pages or the pages of the local network.
fossick’s `local_host` refuses a local name (such as `printer.local`), a
name with no dot, and an address that is not on the internet, with no
DNS look-up.
[`public_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#public_url)
uses `local_host`, then fossick’s `check_url(url, allow_private=False)`:
fossick looks up the host and raises `BlockedURL` for a private address,
and
[`public_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#public_url)
makes it a
[`LinkError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#linkerror).
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link)
uses
[`public_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#public_url)
before it fetches, because a name on the internet can point to a local
address.

The fetch checks again. With `allow_private=False` (from
[`fetch_opts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#fetch_opts)),
fossick looks up the host, refuses a private address, and connects only
to the addresses that it checked. So a host that gives a different
address each time cannot get past the check of the fetch.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L591"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### link_kind

``` python
def link_kind(
    url:str
)->str:
```

*The reader for `url`, as `fossick.what_is` names it: only for an arXiv
id, or an http or https link to a host on the internet. Else
[`LinkError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#linkerror).*

#### Papers from arXiv HTML

The PDF of a paper loses its maths: “scale the dot products by
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$” comes out as “by 1 dk”. arXiv also gives most
papers as an HTML page (made with LaTeXML), at `arxiv.org/html/<id>`.
Each formula on that page has its TeX. So
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link)
reads that page first, and keeps each formula as `$…$` in the text. When
the page is not there, it reads the PDF as before.

The page is text that abhyasa does not trust. abhyasa reads at most
`research.PAGE_BYTES` of it, drops its scripts, styles and menus, and
takes the TeX from the `alttext` (or the TeX annotation) of each MathML
element, never as HTML. The vault keeps the text that the passages come
from, so each passage stays word for word with its source.

fossick’s `arxiv_md` turns the page into markdown. `math_md` is its name
in abhyasa. Each formula becomes a token first, so that the markdown
step cannot change its TeX. Then each token becomes `$TeX$`, or
`$$TeX$$` for a block formula. A numbered equation (a LaTeXML table)
becomes one line with its number. A `$` in the text becomes `\$`, so it
does not start a formula.

[`read_arxiv_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#read_arxiv_html)
calls fossick’s
[`read_arxiv_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#read_arxiv_html).
It fetches the HTML page of paper `aid` one time, with plain HTTP and
the limits of a link. It gives the title, the text and the links of the
figures. It gives None on any error, for a status other than 200, for a
page that is not a LaTeXML paper, and for a page with less than `SHORT`
characters of text. A figure link must be in the folder of the paper on
`arxiv.org/html`.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L624"

### read_arxiv_html

``` python
def read_arxiv_html(
    aid:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*The arXiv HTML page of paper `aid` as `title`, `text` (from `math_md`),
`figures` (links) and `url`, from one plain fetch with the limits of a
link (fossick
[`read_arxiv_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#read_arxiv_html)).
None when there is no usable page.*

[`save_figures`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#save_figures)
saves each figure of the page in the assets folder of the paper, at the
path that its link in the text gives, so
[`figure_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#figure_path)
finds it. It fetches from `arxiv.org` only, at most
`research.PAGE_BYTES` for each figure. The address after the redirects
must be `https` on `arxiv.org` or a subdomain of it. A larger figure is
not saved, so no file is cut short. It keeps a file that is already
there.
[`_file_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_file_html)
files the text on the shelf of papers under `arxiv.org/abs/<id>`. When
that source already has another text, as after a new version of the
paper, the new text gets its own source key, so the passages of an old
walk keep their source.
[`_paper_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_paper_html)
does both for
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link).
A test gives its own `html`, so no figure is fetched.

`read(how, target, **kw)` does the fetch. The default calls the `Vault`
method `how` on the shelf of the link, after it looks up the host. A web
page uses plain HTTP only (`auto=False`). A page that only a browser can
read gives no page, because a browser runs the scripts of the page. A
docs site can redirect its start page to another host or folder, as
`ai.pydantic.dev` and `docs.claude.com` do. For a crawl, `final(url)`
fetches the start page one time and gives its address after the
redirects. The folder is taken from that address, and its host is
checked like the first one: a host on this computer or the local network
is refused. A redirect to a folder name such as `.../overview/` names
the overview page, so the folder is the one above it. A locale folder
such as `/docs/en/` or `/docs/pt-BR/` is the folder. A locale is a
language code (ISO 639-1), so `/docs/go/` is not one. A redirect on the
same host to a folder above the folder of the link, such as the bare
host root, keeps the folder of the link. Some pages lose almost all
their text in the reader.
[`_whole`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_whole)
files such a page again with all its text. A link with almost no text in
all its pages gives a message, not an empty walk. A test gives a fake
`read`, so the test does not use the network.

### file_link

``` python
def file_link(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, url:str, max_pages:int=None, read:NoneType=None, final:NoneType=None,
    title_of:NoneType=None, html:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*File the pages of `url` in the vault. Return `shelf`, `doc_id`, `title`
and `url` of each page in the folder of `url` (after any redirect of the
start page), in reading order, at most `max_pages` (default: the setting
`links.pages`). `final(url)` gives the address after the redirects. A
paper filed under its arXiv id gets its real title from `title_of(id)`
(with the real readers,
[`arxiv_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#arxiv_title)).
An arXiv paper is read from `html(id)` first (with the real readers,
[`read_arxiv_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#read_arxiv_html)),
and from its PDF when that gives None.*

Each fetch refuses a private address, also when
`FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1` is set.
[`_final`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_final)
fetches `127.0.0.1` here, and fossick refuses it before it connects.

``` python
import os, fossick
```

``` python
was = os.environ.get('FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE'); os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE'] = '1'
try:
    test_eq(fetch_opts()['allow_private'], False)
    test_fail(lambda: _final('http://127.0.0.1:9/'), exc=fossick.BlockedURL)
finally:
    if was is None: os.environ.pop('FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE', None)
    else: os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE'] = was
```

The tests of links below use these imports.

``` python
import fossick
```

``` python
from fossick.core import Selector
```

`link_folder` gives the folder of a link. `in_scope` keeps a link in
that folder. It refuses a link on a host that only starts with the same
name, and a path with `..`, also when the `..` is in percent codes such
as `%2e%2e`.

``` python
START = 'https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/overview'
test_eq(link_folder(START), 'https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/')
test_eq(link_folder('https://ai.pydantic.dev'), 'https://ai.pydantic.dev/')
assert in_scope('https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/setup#a', START) and not in_scope('https://docs.example.dev/en/api/x', START)
assert not in_scope('https://evil.example/en/docs/tool/x', START) and not in_scope('https://docs.example.dev.evil.example/en/docs/tool/', START)
assert not in_scope('https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/../../admin', START)
for up in ('%2e%2e', '%2E%2E', '.%2e', '%2E.', '%252e%252e'):   # a `..` in percent codes, which many servers decode
    assert not in_scope(f'https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/{up}/{up}/private', START), up
assert in_scope('https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/my%20page', START) and in_scope('https://docs.example.dev/my%20docs/a', 'https://docs.example.dev/my docs/')
```

[`link_kind`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#link_kind)
takes only an arXiv id, or an http or https link to a host on the
internet. It refuses a file, this computer and the local network. It
also refuses a video link. Each refusal is a
[`LinkError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#linkerror),
so the app can show its words to you.

``` python
test_eq(link_kind('1706.03762'), 'arxiv')
test_eq(link_kind(START), 'web')
test_eq(link_kind('https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcore'), 'github')
for bad in ('file:///etc/passwd', '/etc/passwd', 'ftp://example.com/a', 'http://localhost:5001/', 'http://127.0.0.1/', 'http://127.1/',
            'http://[::1]/', 'http://10.0.0.5/x', 'http://192.168.1.1/', 'http://169.254.169.254/latest', 'http://router/', 'http://nas.local/'):
    test_fail(lambda: link_kind(bad), exc=LinkError)
test_fail(lambda: link_kind('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x'), contains='video', exc=LinkError)
```

### as_link

``` python
def as_link(
    s:str
)->str | None:
```

*The link in the field `s`: a web link, an arXiv id, `arxiv:<id>` or an
arXiv address. None for anything else, such as a vault name.*

A web link, an arXiv id and an arXiv address are links. A vault name or
a title is not a link:

``` python
test_eq(as_link(' https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762 '), 'https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762')
test_eq(as_link('1706.03762'), '1706.03762')
test_eq(as_link('arXiv: 1706.03762v2'), '1706.03762v2')
test_eq(as_link('arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762'), 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762')
for name in ('Rasi Characteristics', '3df4abc4deb9f8b0', '/tmp/attention.pdf', 'file:///etc/passwd', 'javascript:alert(1)', ''): test_is(as_link(name), None)
```

An arXiv link and a PDF link are papers. A docs site is not a paper:

``` python
for u in ('1706.03762', 'https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762', 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762v7', 'https://example.org/a/paper.PDF?x=1'): assert is_paper(u), u
for u in ('https://docs.example.dev/attention/', 'https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcore', 'Rasi Characteristics', '/tmp/a.pdf', ''): assert not is_paper(u), u
```

[`reading_order`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#reading_order)
puts the start page first, then the pages in the order of their first
link on the start page. A page with no link stays at the end.

``` python
pg = lambda u: AttrDict(url=f'https://d.dev/docs/{u}')
test_eq(reading_order([pg('a'), pg('x'), pg('c'), pg('b')], 'See [B](b#top), [C](/docs/c) and [B again](b).').attrgot('url'),
        [pg(u).url for u in 'abcx'])
```

A fake reader takes the place of the network. It files four pages: the
start page, two pages in its folder, and one blog page outside it.

``` python
SITE = {START: '# Overview\n\nSee [Setup](/en/docs/tool/setup) and [Hooks](/en/docs/tool/hooks).',
        'https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/hooks': '# Hooks\n\nA hook runs a command at a set point.',
        'https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/setup': '# Setup\n\nInstall the tool with one command.',
        'https://docs.example.dev/blog/news': '# News\n\nWe have a new logo.'}
calls = []
def fake_read(lr):
    "File every page of SITE in crawl order, and keep the call."
    def read(how, target, **kw):
        calls.append((how, target, kw))
        return [lr.vault.add(md, md.split('\n')[0][2:], source=u, kind='web', meta=dict(url=u)) for u, md in SITE.items()]
    return read
```

The crawl gets the folder and the page cap, and the walk does not use
the blog page. A cap of 1 reads one page. An arXiv id uses the arXiv
reader. A link with no pages gives a clear message.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
docs = file_link(lr, START, max_pages=500, read=fake_read(lr))
test_eq((calls[0][0], calls[0][2]['max_pages']), ('crawl', val('links.cap')))
test_eq(link_folder(calls[0][2]['scope']), 'https://docs.example.dev/en/docs/tool/')   # the crawl keeps to the folder of the link
test_eq([d.title for d in docs], ['Overview', 'Setup', 'Hooks'])        # the start page, then its links in order; no blog page
test_eq(docs[0].shelf, 'store')
calls.clear(); test_eq(len(file_link(lr, START, max_pages=1, read=fake_read(lr))), 1); test_eq(calls[0][0], 'url')
calls.clear(); file_link(lr, '1706.03762', read=fake_read(lr)); test_eq(calls[0][:2], ('pdf', 'https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762'))   # the PDF, not the abstract
test_fail(lambda: file_link(temp_learning(), START, read=lambda how, target, **kw: []), contains='could not read')
```

A paper that the PDF reader filed under its arXiv id gets the real title
of the paper. A paper that has a real title keeps it.

``` python
TEXT = '# Attention\n\nSee the paper. ' * 30
def paper(url, title, **kw):
    "The title of the one page that `file_link` gives for a paper that a reader filed under `title`."
    l = temp_learning()
    return file_link(l, url, read=lambda how, target, **k: [l.vault.add(TEXT, title, source=target, kind='pdf')], **kw)[0].title
test_eq(paper('1706.03762', '1706.03762', title_of=lambda i: 'Attention Is All You Need'), 'Attention Is All You Need')
test_eq(paper('https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762v7', '1706.03762v7.pdf', title_of=lambda i: i + ' paper'), '1706.03762v7 paper')   # the id with its version
test_eq(paper('1706.03762', 'Attention', title_of=lambda i: 'Other'), 'Attention')
test_eq(paper('1706.03762', '1706.03762', title_of=lambda i: None), '1706.03762')   # no title to give: the id stays
test_eq(paper('hep-th/9901001v2', '9901001v2.pdf', title_of=lambda i: 'Old ' + i), 'Old hep-th/9901001v2')   # the old form of an id
test_eq(paper('https://arxiv.org/abs/math.GT/0601001', '0601001', title_of=lambda i: 'Old ' + i), 'Old math.GT/0601001')
test_eq([arxiv_ref(u) for u in ('https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601001.pdf', 'arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9901001v2', 'https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7')], ['math/0601001', 'hep-th/9901001v2', '1706.03762v7'])
test_eq([as_link(s) for s in ('math/0601001', 'arXiv:hep-th/9901001v2')], ['math/0601001', 'hep-th/9901001v2'])
test_eq(is_paper('math/0601001'), True); test_eq(is_paper('docs/2024'), False)
test_eq(is_id_title('0601001', 'math/0601001'), True); test_eq(is_id_title('0601001'), False)
from unittest.mock import patch as mock_patch
with mock_patch('fossick.read_arxiv', return_value=dict(title='word ' * 80)): t = arxiv_title('1706.03762')
assert len(t) <= 201 and t.endswith('word…')   # cut at a word
with mock_patch('fossick.read_arxiv', return_value=dict(title='  A  short\ntitle ')): test_eq(arxiv_title('1706.03762'), 'A short title')
test_eq([is_id_title(t) for t in ('1706.03762', 'arXiv:1706.03762v5', '1706.03762.pdf', 'Attention', '', None)], [True, True, True, False, False, False])
```
