#### A tight passage

A quote from a transcript is 1 to 3 whole sentences that name the idea.
[`tight_span`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#tight_span)
cuts at the ends of sentences only, so the passage stays word for word.
A part at the end with no stop is not a sentence.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L1549"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### tight_span

``` python
def tight_span(
    text:str, c, most:int=3
)->str:
```

*1 to `most` whole sentences of `text` on the idea `c`, word for word,
with white space made single spaces: the sentence that names* the idea
best (its name or a key term, then its words:
[`idea_words`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#idea_words),
then the words of its statement), and the next sentences while they name
a word of the idea too in 6 words or more, or while the span is shorter
than `SPAN_SHORT`, up to `MOST` characters. The flat `text` when it has
no whole sentence.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L1541"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### sentences

``` python
def sentences(
    text:str
)->list:
```

*The whole sentences of `text` as `(start, end)`: each one ends with a
stop before a capital or the end. A part at the end with no stop is not
a sentence.*

The span of *softmax* is the sentence that names it best, and the next
sentence that names it too. The span is in the text word for word, and a
text with no stop stays as it is.

``` python
sp = tight_span(TALK, dict(name='Softmax', statement='Softmax turns scores into weights that add up to one.'))
test_eq(sp, 'So softmax turns a list of scores into weights that add up to one. And you know, the biggest score gets the biggest weight, so we can see what the model looks at.')
assert sp in TALK and 1 <= len(sentences(sp)) <= 3
test_eq(tight_span('so this is, you know,', dict(name='Softmax')), 'so this is, you know,')
```

#### Links to the lesson

A transcript links to the notebooks of its repo that its summary or its
text names, by file stem, by *name notebook* or by first heading, else
to the notebooks that share its ideas. It never guesses from the lesson
number. It also links to its summary (`lesson17-summ0` next to
`lesson17`), and to its video. A transcript with a YouTube link opens
the video at the time stamp before the passage (fossick `yt_link`). With
no link, the video link is a YouTube search for the course and the
lesson, and a file next to the transcript can name the playlist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L1680"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### stamp_before

``` python
def stamp_before(
    text:str, at:int
)->int | None:
```

*The seconds of the last time stamp in `text` before the place `at`, or
None when there is none.*

A time stamp at the start of a line or in brackets counts, and the last
one before the passage gives its time. The course name comes from
*Lesson 3 of …*.

``` python
test_eq(stamp_before('[00:01] Hi. [01:05] Softmax turns scores into weights.', 20), 65)
test_eq(stamp_before('Scores of 3:1 are not a time.', 20), None)
test_eq(course_of(TALK), 'Deep Learning for Coders')
test_eq(video_link(AttrDict(url='https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ', lesson=3), 65).url, 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&t=65s')
test_eq(video_link(AttrDict(url='', lesson=3), course='Deep Learning for Coders').url, SEARCH + 'Deep+Learning+for+Coders+Lesson+3')
```

A lesson names a notebook by its file stem, by *name notebook*, or by
its title. A stem with no number, such as `segmentation`, is too common
a word to count alone.

``` python
test_eq(nb_names(AttrDict(title='nbs/11_initializing'), 'initialization'), ['11_initializing', 'initializing notebook', 'initialization'])
test_eq(nb_names(AttrDict(title='nbs/segmentation')), ['segmentation notebook'])
test_eq(_first_at('then the lesson shows accelerated sgd.', ['accelerated sgd']), 22)
```

#### The passage and its rank

[`transcript_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#transcript_read)
is the step `read` as the page shows it: the tight span, the label
*Lecture transcript · Lesson 3*, and the links.
[`transcripts_last`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#transcripts_last)
puts a transcript after a notebook or a doc that is just as good.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L1709"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->list:
```

*The passages `ps` in their order, but a passage from a transcript goes
after each other passage that is just as `good` (a key, default 0* for

### transcript_read

``` python
def transcript_read(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, read, c:NoneType=None
)->dict:
```

*The `read` of a step as the page shows it. A passage from a lecture
transcript becomes a tight span
([`tight_span`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#tight_span),
word for word), with* `what` = `Lecture transcript · Lesson 17` and
`links` to the lesson notebook and the video, at the time of the passage
when the transcript has time stamps. Any other `read` stays as it is.
Nothing is saved.

#### The page of a transcript

The vault page of a transcript has a title, its links, a short list of
topics and the text in paragraphs. A topic comes from the summary when
the vault has one, else from the ideas that a walk took from the
transcript. Each topic jumps to the paragraph where it starts: the one
that names its rare words, near its share of the talk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L1762"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### transcript_page

``` python
def transcript_page(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, shelf:str, doc_id:str, text:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*What the vault page of a lecture transcript shows above its text:
`title` (`Lecture transcript · Lesson 17`), `links`
([`transcript_links`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#transcript_links)*
with the summary and the playlist), `topics` with `where` they come
from, and `paras`, the text in paragraphs. None for any other document.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L1747"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### topics_of

``` python
def topics_of(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, t, paras
)->tuple:
```

*The topics of transcript `t` with the paragraph of `paras` where each
one starts, as `(where, [(topic, paragraph)])`. From its summary* (the
first sentence of each part) when the vault has one, else from the ideas
that a walk took from it (their names), in the order of the talk.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L1732"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### jump_places

``` python
def jump_places(
    paras, topics
)->list:
```

*For each topic of `topics` (a text), the paragraph of `paras` where it
starts: the one that names the most of its rare words, near its* share
of the talk (topic 3 of 8 is near paragraph 3/8 of the way), and at or
after the paragraph of the topic before it. A summary keeps the order of
the talk. A word that many paragraphs have counts less.

Three topics go to the paragraphs that name them, in order.

``` python
PS = ['Hi and welcome. Today is about attention.', 'Softmax turns scores into weights.', 'The weights mix the values.', 'Next week is about training.']
test_eq(jump_places(PS, ['How softmax makes weights.', 'How weights mix values.', 'What comes next week.']), [1, 2, 3])
```
